bugs.title: VEC media flickers, video fails to trigger, and player can freeze
bugs.symptom: The active VEC visual can freeze on a single frame while playback continues. The latest recurrence is on iPhone Safari mobile after three solid songs: artwork was initially missing, a video started, and the following video froze during its handoff on Girls on Bikes around 0:32 / 5:10.
affected_examples: Post-closure mobile recurrence: Girls on Bikes froze around 0:32 / 5:10 on iPhone Safari after missing artwork, first video startup, and the next-video handoff
Post-continuity3: She's My Guru froze at ~0:48 on desktop
Live frameheartbeat1 reproduction: She's My Guru remained in TRANSITIONING at ~0:33 and ~0:59 with the same ended 10-second video, two played assets, and zero failed
Post-continuity2: Dirty Bird froze at ~0:30 on desktop
Post-continuity2: Right Between the Eyes froze at ~0:28 on desktop
Right Between the Eyes video froze at ~0:53 on 2026-08-18
Dirty Bird video froze at ~2:45 on 2026-08-19 while audio and controls continued
Where Next? first froze at ~2:40 on 2026-08-19; screenshot at 3:00/3:59 showed audio and interface continuing with the same frozen frame
Mr. Top Mi Up video froze at ~2:00 on 2026-08-19 during rollout of the continuity build
Firefox desktop missing graphics and videos on 2026-08-17
working_comparisons: Audio continues normally during the frozen video
Interface controls remain responsive during the frozen video
Normal pool exhaustion is designed to clear played state and reuse the eligible pool
Where Next? full-duration live run on continuity2 passed ~2:40, reached 3:54 with 16 played/0 failed assets, and auto-advanced with VEC active
Direct mobile comparison remained visually flawless beyond 3:35 while desktop continued to reproduce
Continuity3 live desktop check: Dirty Bird passed 0:30 and reached ~1:08 with seven assets played and zero failed
Continuity3 live desktop check: Right Between the Eyes passed 0:28 and reached ~0:31 with three assets played and zero failed
Continuity5 live desktop check: She's My Guru reached ~1:13 with six played assets, zero failed, and no stuck TRANSITIONING state
User continuity5 desktop test: one newly played song completed 100% with flowing VEC video
User continuity5 desktop test: older catalog song Do You Love Me? passed the 2:00 to 2:45 failure zone and completed 100% with smooth video
Immediately before the mobile recurrence, three consecutive songs completed with solid visual playback
bugs.root_cause: Live She's My Guru runs reproduced the desktop engine stuck in TRANSITIONING while audio continued. advance() held the serialized advancing lock while awaiting either the shared next-asset preload chain or a prepared video's play() promise. A slow preload could span sequential asset timeouts, while a prepared video could return a play promise that never settled. Lease and watchdog recovery calls then returned because advancing was already true, leaving the same ended video visible. Normal pool exhaustion is not the cause. The 2026-08-19 mobile recurrence is not yet proven to share this desktop cause. Its missing-artwork to video to frozen-next-video sequence requires inspection of the mobile transition lifecycle and iPhone Safari media state. The mobile artwork authority also cleared the stage while validating exact 9x16 artwork. The mobile motion runtime reused one video element across clip URLs and relied on timeupdate progress, which does not prove iPhone Safari is presenting new frames.
bugs.fix_summary: Continuity5 removes the old current layer before every replacement start, caps transition preload waiting at 2.6 seconds, caps a prepared video's play promise at 1.6 seconds, and prevents abandoned preload work from reinserting stale nodes. Live verification reached ~1:13 on She's My Guru with six handoffs and zero failed assets. User verification included multiple complete desktop songs: one new song and Do You Love Me?, which passed the prior 2:00 to 2:45 failure zone and completed 100% smoothly. The user marked the repair verified and closed it on 2026-08-19. Mobile is unchanged. The later Girls on Bikes mobile freeze reopened the bug on 2026-08-19. The prior desktop verification remains historical evidence, but mobile is now active scope. Mobilecontinuity1 keeps provisional artwork visible, replaces the video element at every clip handoff, watches presented frames with requestVideoFrameCallback, and advances after 3.2 seconds without a new frame. The cache-busted build was published on 2026-08-19. Mobile user verification is pending.
bugs.future_repair: Test at least four consecutive songs on iPhone Safari, prioritizing Girls on Bikes. Verify artwork remains visible before the first video, every next-video handoff produces moving frames, and any presentation stall advances within 3.2 seconds. If it returns, capture StashboxMobileVecVideoRuntime.state(), the active URL, videoTime, lastPresentedFrameAt, and lastPresentedMediaTime before changing the runtime.

bugs.title: Profile listening stats do not advance with desktop listening
bugs.symptom: Profile Songs Played remained stuck at 191 after additional logged-in desktop listening; Hours Listened could undercount because it uses the same authenticated history source.
affected_examples: DEV V2 clean desktop logged-in listening
Profile Songs Played stuck at 191
working_comparisons: Favorites direct user_favorites count
After repair user observed Songs Played advance from 191 to 195
bugs.root_cause: Clean desktop public play qualification and authenticated profile history used separate persistence/detection paths. Public v2-play-tracker.js could qualify /radio/track plays while desktop did not reliably write matching user_listening_history rows. Profile stats also cached the first loaded stats object and did not automatically refetch.
bugs.fix_summary: Profile stats now refetch on return/focus/visibility. Desktop authenticated history is bridged directly from the canonical stashbox:qualified-play event, preserving the same qualified song/session and writing /radio/me/history on finalize. The independent desktop history owner was removed and bridge sends were made session-independent.
bugs.future_repair: Confirm stashbox:qualified-play fires, then trace desktop-profile-history-bridge.js to /radio/me/history and /radio/me/profile-stats. Do not add a second play-threshold tracker. Hours Listened remains monitored because historical desktop gaps are not reconstructed.

bugs.title: Fast login fails with missing USERNAME on mobile and desktop
bugs.symptom: After the fast-login optimization, both mobile and desktop returned `Missing required parameter USERNAME` despite populated email and password fields.
affected_examples: DEV V2 desktop login
DEV V2 mobile login
working_comparisons: Normal Cognito credential validation after the corrected request sequence
bugs.root_cause: The initial fast-login path prewarmed the login auth guard before the user's email/username was available. That anonymous guard request could fail with a missing USERNAME requirement even though the direct Cognito InitiateAuth payload already had the correct USERNAME/PASSWORD structure.
bugs.fix_summary: Fast login now preloads only auth configuration while the user is typing. The login guard runs only on submit with the real email supplied as username and email, blank credentials are blocked before AWS calls, Cognito receives AuthParameters USERNAME/PASSWORD, and bounded timeout plus immediate-success behavior are retained. User verified successful login on desktop and mobile.
bugs.future_repair: If this returns, inspect request ordering first. Never call the login guard without the actual email/username. Preserve config prewarming, and keep credential-dependent guard/Cognito calls on submit with real credentials.
